clue.text: Lifetime is short and about to be over

indicators.note: something short is missing its end, so the last letter of the word for lifetime is cut away

parts.note: a lifetime is a life span
RE means about or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A gloomy reflection that life is brief and nearly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifetime is short' reads as a sad remark but means the word for lifetime is cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare means left over or surplus, so it can replace over in a phrase like 'food left over'.

clue.text: Imagine guarding missile plant

indicators.note: a guard surrounds what it protects, so one word sits around the other

parts.note: to see something in your mind is to imagine it
SAM is a surface-to-air missile

explanation.surface: A fantasy of a missile emplacement being protected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missile plant' reads as a weapons factory; plant is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame is a herbaceous plant grown for its oil-rich seeds.

clue.text: Over pit, knock back forcibly

parts.note: to do something over is to do it again
the pit of a fruit is its stone
to knock back a drink is to swill it

explanation.surface: Someone forced to gulp a drink down over a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something against one's will means under compulsion, which is the adverbial sense of forcibly.

clue.text: Find oneself often duplicating content

indicators.note: content is what is held inside, so the letters lie within the neighbouring words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone discovers they keep copying things.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up somewhere is to find oneself there eventually, an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: Dad is gone, "being distraught" identified

indicators.note: a distraught state is a disordered one, so these letters get jumbled

parts.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A grieving person's condition after a father's death is put into words.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who has diagnosed an illness has identified it, a close synonym in medical use.

clue.text: Risk capital?

parts.note: surface reading: venture funds invested in a speculative business; setter's reading: extra pay earned for taking on hazardous work

explanation.walkthrough: Risk capital is a finance term for venture investment; the question mark invites reading it as cash paid for running a risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Danger money is a wage premium for hazardous work, literally money earned by taking risks.

clue.text: A daughter's love for song and dance

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A girl's fondness for musical theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A song and dance is an idiom for a needless fuss, which is what ado means.

clue.text: Primitive old lady in news, not a complete success

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the letters supplied by the final word

parts.note: news read as more than one 'new', each N; this is the first
primitive things are early in development
a mother, colloquially one's old lady

explanation.surface: An elderly woman from prehistory makes the headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: News is read as the plural of new, so it supplies two Ns, one on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: A nearly man is someone who repeatedly comes close to success without achieving it.

clue.text: Web designer keeping habit that's uncultivated for priest?

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the following pieces sit within

parts.note: a spider spins and designs webs
a habitual routine is a ritual
a lea is grassland or fallow ground left untilled

explanation.surface: An arachnid's web wrapped around a nun's habit, oddly asking about priests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' suggests a religious garment, nudging towards the priest theme, but here it is a routine. A lea is meadow left unploughed.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is one example of a spiritual leader, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Fantastic chap turned into unlikely deity

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so the word for chap reads backwards
into places one piece inside the other
unlikely suggests an improbable form, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man improbably transformed into a god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned into' reads as one phrase meaning became, but turned reverses the chap and into places him inside the rearranged god.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamite is informal praise for something excellent or sensational, a slang equivalent of fantastic.

clue.text: A raised hand

parts.note: surface reading: someone putting a hand up, to ask or vote; setter's reading: a hand, meaning a round of applause, given by an audience on its feet

explanation.walkthrough: To give someone a big hand is to applaud them; a raised one comes from an audience that has stood up.
explanation.definitionFit: This ovation is applause delivered by a crowd rising to its feet, so it is clapping from an elevated position.

clue.text: Band of priests, like boy band, embracing pop

indicators.note: an embrace wraps around something, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: a boy band is all male
to pop out quickly is to nip out

explanation.surface: A clerical group compared to a pop boy band.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'band' twice: once in the definition as a strip of cloth, once in the boy band that is all male. Pop means nip, as in pop to the shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A maniple is a strip of silk worn on the left arm by a priest at Mass, so a band of priests' vestments.

clue.text: A metal coin oddly buried by Scotsman

indicators.note: something buried is enclosed, so it goes inside the name

parts.note: Calum is a typically Scottish man's name

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in odd positions of the word

parts.note: first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: A Scot burying a metal coin, perhaps as treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A metal coin' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Calcium is a soft grey alkaline-earth element, one of the metals.

clue.text: Author into rice salad, nuts, cooked with sugar

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the author of the clue refers to themself as me
taken as written, fodder

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: nuts in a rice salad, glazed with sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramelised food has been heated with sugar until it browns.

clue.text: Flag from castle found in ship

indicators.note: found in says one piece is located inside another

parts.note: a steamer is a steamship
castle is another name for the rook in chess, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: A banner taken from a castle discovered aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow pennant or flag flown from a mast.

clue.text: Cream that is applied to bad girl in part of hospital

indicators.note: in puts the combined pieces inside the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
a moll is a gangster's girlfriend
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An ointment rubbed on a troublesome patient on a ward.
explanation.walkthrough: A moll is a gangster's girlfriend, a stock crossword bad girl.
explanation.definitionFit: An emollient is a soothing, softening skin preparation, such as a cream.

clue.text: Opening pieces of music occupy us near the stage

indicators.note: the opening piece of each word is its first letter

parts.note: initials of the five words

explanation.surface: The overture and its players settle in near the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount a production is to stage it, both verbs meaning to put on a show.

clue.text: Those boring fights interrupted by commercial material

indicators.note: an interruption breaks into the middle, so a piece goes inside

parts.note: brawls are rough fights
an advertisement, commercial material in print or broadcast

explanation.surface: Dull scuffles broken up by advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' wants to mean dull; here it means drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bradawls are small pointed tools for making holes in wood, so they bore.

clue.text: Start to record, playing the same piece of music

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter
something playing is on
DO is short for ditto, the same

explanation.surface: A musician begins recording and repeats the same track.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form in which a recurring theme alternates with episodes.

clue.text: Noun I'm on about — also short noun phrases

indicators.note: about suggests turning round, so the preceding letters run backwards

parts.note: N is the grammatical abbreviation for noun
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grammarian rambling about nouns and short phrases.
explanation.walkthrough: N, IM and ON together read backwards, then ALSO loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, nominals are words or phrases that function as nouns.

clue.text: Smell of sulphur on fish

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
a tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Fish that smells of sulphur, like rotten eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong, unpleasant odour.

clue.text: I had returned fan's present

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters read in the opposite direction

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
to splay is to spread out, as a fan does

explanation.surface: Someone returned an admirer's gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan's' and 'present' tempt a reading as an admirer's gift; fan is really a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To display something is to present it for viewing, both verbs.

clue.text: "Knock" and "knack" — brilliant

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
a bent is a natural aptitude or knack

explanation.surface: Two similar-sounding words are praised as brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes light that flickers softly or a wit that glows, so radiantly bright.

clue.text: Radioactive material in insect trap

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a moth is a winged insect
U is the symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Uranium caught in a bug trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insect trap' reads as one thing; trap is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Trap is slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.

clue.text: He's mad, but Winner's put out film about racism

indicators.note: put out means upset or disturbed, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: Director Michael Winner is annoyed and angry about a controversial film.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Winner was an English film director, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: White Man's Burden is a 1995 film reversing racial roles, named after Kipling's poem on imperialism.

clue.text: It comes from volcano while hot

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I was leaving'
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A volcano spews something while scorching.
explanation.definitionFit: Volcanic ash is the fine debris thrown out by an eruption.

clue.text: Roughly marked patch about to be put in outhouse

indicators.note: put in places the preceding pieces inside the following word

parts.note: a shed is an outbuilding
a patch of ground is a plot
C for circa, about

explanation.surface: A patch put inside a garden shed leaves rough marks.
explanation.walkthrough: C stands for circa, Latin for about.
explanation.definitionFit: Splotched means covered in irregular blotches or rough spots.

clue.text: Croaking right into pig's ear

indicators.note: into places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a pig's ear is British slang for a botched job, a mess or hash
R for right

explanation.surface: A frog's croak heard right in a pig's ear.
explanation.walkthrough: To make a pig's ear of something is British slang for botching it; making a hash of it means the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh voice is rough and grating, like a croaking one.
